messages:
dani-support: heads up — acme-inc reported repeated streaming failures when using the hosted API. They get a broken pipe on the client after ~18s and we mark the request as 5xx and bill them. sample req_id: req_zx17
acme-cs: reproducer from their side (node fetch):
```js
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer sk-acme-123' },
  body: chunkedBodyStream() // client streams prompts
});
// client sees socket error: write EPIPE after ~18s
```
dani-support: they say it used to work, spike started yesterday after ~15:00 UTC. billing team flagged charged tokens on these failures.
trent-sre: thanks. any gateway logs / upstream messages? can you paste trace_id and edge logs?
acme-cs: trace: tz-req-0001. gateway logs show: 
```
ERROR write: broken pipe
gateway: upstream_reset: FIN_WHILE_WRITING
mark_response(5xx) -> billing_counter++
```
kayla-eng: FIN_WHILE_WRITING suggests client closed while we were still sending. but we shouldn't treat as gateway 5xx for billing. looks like our upstream classification lumps this into 502.
trent-sre: agree. reclass heuristics: if client half-close/FIN then we should mark as client_abort, not server_error. need to check egress path that maps upstream reset to 5xx.
mike-billing: invoiced customer already — disputed. if we reclass, need retro bill adjustments. opened INC-4532.
jenna-devex: can we get a short repro we can run internally? acme provided a small script that streams a few chunks then force-close the socket. I'll attach with curl variant.
dani-support: acme test script (curl):
```bash
# server streams but client halves after 18s to simulate mobile proxy
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-123" -X POST -d @chunks.txt https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams
# then client sends FIN (kill -9)
```
kayla-eng: I'll try to reproduce in staging. initial hypothesis: a keepalive/halfclose race between proxy and gateway where gateway is still writing trailing chunk/trailer and then sees FIN; our code treats that as an upstream error (server-side) instead of client abort. also potential chunked encoding trailer loss.
trent-sre: log snippet from edge around tz-req-0001: 
```
[edge] 2024-08-21T15:02:17Z conn=345 write_loop: wrote 512 bytes
[edge] 2024-08-21T15:02:35Z conn=345 read: got FIN from client
[edge] 2024-08-21T15:02:35Z conn=345 upstream_write: EPIPE
[edge] 2024-08-21T15:02:35Z conn=345 classify: upstream_reset -> 502
```
kayla-eng: that matches. workaround might be buffering last chunk or catching EPIPE and mapping to client_abort. but need to ensure we don't mask real upstream errors.
mike-billing: timeline: billed on 2024-08-21 15:03 UTC for tokens after the FIN event. customer is asking for credit if reclassification happens.
trent-sre: quick patch idea: if we detect client FIN immediately prior to EPIPE (within 1s), classify as client_abort. low risk and targets this regression window. can ship to staging for a day.
jenna-devex: can we add a metric and dashboard for "client-halfclose-eips" and count occurrences by route/model so we can scope impact?
kayla-eng: yes. I'll add a trace and a Prometheus counter: edge.client_halfclose_eip_count{route="/v1/streams"}.
dani-support: acme wants ETA for fix and billing action. propose: repro + staging patch today, limited prod rollout tomorrow, billing credit pending reclassification results.
mike-billing: ok I created billing ticket BILL-9877 and put tentative credit hold. will wait for eng confirmation.
trent-sre: I pushed a quick non-blocking classifier in staging that treats EPIPE with recent client-FIN as client_abort. deploying now. deploy-bot: deployed edge v3.14.2-staging to staging-cluster at 2024-08-21T18:40:00Z. :rocket:
deploy-bot: canary 3/3 healthy.
kayla-eng: ran the acme repro against staging — reproduced and classifier now returns client_abort and we do not increment 5xx counters. logs: 
```
[edge] classify: client_fin_detected -> mark_client_abort
[edge] billing: no_charge_for_client_abort
```
acme-cs: tested staging and verified client sees broken pipe but wasn't charged on our side. thanks. :sparkles:
dani-support: next steps: kayla to schedule prod rollout tomorrow morning UTC; trent to coordinate rollback plan; mike to keep billing hold until post-rollout audit; jenna to create dashboard. I'll update acme with this plan and time estimate. :thumbsup:
trent-sre: adding a followup to run a backfill script to re-evaluate recent 24h events and generate list of requests for possible credit. will share results in INC-4532.
mike-billing: thanks all. I'll pause invoices for acme until we confirm.
jenna-devex: documenting the repro and the heuristic in internal runbook: docs/streaming/halfclose-classification.md (draft).
